# Dena Acosta Beere
# Building a Better Concord,
For All of Us.
Meet Dena Acosta Beere
### Meet Dena Acosta Beere
Dena Acosta Beere is an active volunteer and leader in our District, always willing to lend a helping hand to protect families, improve safety, and make services more accessible. Dena led the effort to install three new pedestrian crosswalks at Market and Meadow Streets, improving pedestrian and road safety for our residents.
Dena served on the County Commission for Women and Girls, the Mt. Diablo USD Parent Advisory Committee, and was appointed by Supervisor Ken Carlson as a Community Advisory Board Member for Measure X, where she assesses health and safety needs and recommends funding priorities.
A graduate of Stanford University, Dena worked in commercial and residential real estate, specializing in helping first-time home buyers. Her professional skills give Dena a firm grasp on the complex issues that come before the city council. Her collaborative approach brings disparate groups together to find common ground and improve outcomes.
You will find Dena and her husband, a firefighter, along with their two small children, enjoying Concord’s parks and playgrounds, eating at the diverse restaurants in District 3, and being involved in community events.
While Dena’s skills are unique to the council, they are not unique to those doing the work in our neighborhoods to make Concord better for our families.
## Dena's Priorities
Dena Acosta Beere will prioritize policies and programs that improve quality of life, combat the cost of living crisis, and bring equitable programs and services to the diverse neighborhoods of District 3.
Dena and Concord Vice Mayor Dominic Aliano.
## Safety and Quality of Life
As the cost of living impacts families, Concord needs to ensure that city services are maintained and meet community needs. Our families depend on responsive emergency services, better roads, clean parks and playgrounds, and recreation programs for seniors and children, including the Community Youth Center. Many residents do not have cars, making pedestrian and bike safety a top priority.
## Economic Development
District 3 is a dynamic and diverse community and home to thriving local businesses. More can be done to expand code enforcement and fight blight. To fill vacant properties and boost the local economy, permitting should be streamlined, zoning laws and incentives should align, and the collaboration between local business networks should be strengthened.
## Housing
We need to address housing affordability by preventing displacement by maintaining rent stabilization ordinances, improving tenant protections, and building more housing at all levels of affordability.
## Governance
Community voices must be heard and reflected in council priorities. This includes proactive outreach and attending District events to listen to residents, making sure decisions are transparent, and maintaining fiscal stability to ensure public services are maintained.

## District 3 Elect Dena Acosta-Beere
"Acosta-Beere is the best prepared. A former real estate agent, she also serves on Contra Costa County’s community advisory board for its Measure X sales tax and on a Mt. Diablo school district Parent Advisory Committee.
She cut her political teeth in Concord successfully advocating for crosswalks at a busy intersection in her neighborhood. And on the city’s biggest issue, she understands the history of the weapons station master developer and the importance of completing the project.” See the full article here >>
